title: Tanvi Patri, 15, First Indian Woman to Reach Youth Olympic Badminton Final
excerpt: The Odisha shuttler beat Japan's second seed Yuzuno Watanabe 21-14, 11-21, 21-19 in 54 minutes, assuring India its first women's singles medal at the Youth Olympic Games. China's Yi Xin Zhang awaits in the final.
body:
• Fifteen-year-old Tanvi Patri beat Japan's second seed Yuzuno Watanabe 21-14, 11-21, 21-19 in a 54-minute semifinal to become the first Indian woman to reach a Youth Olympic Games badminton final.
  • The win guarantees India its first-ever women's singles badminton medal at the Youth Olympic Games — at least a silver is now assured.
  • Patri, from Odisha and a former U15 and U17 Asian champion, now faces China's Yi Xin Zhang, the reigning World Junior champion, in the gold-medal match.
  • She joins HS Prannoy (silver, Singapore 2010) and Lakshya Sen (silver, Buenos Aires 2018) as the only Indians to reach a Youth Olympic badminton final.

Fifteen-year-old Tanvi Patri has made Indian sporting history, becoming the first Indian woman to reach the badminton final at the Youth Olympic Games. The Indian shuttler defeated Japan's second seed Yuzuno Watanabe in a hard-fought three-game semifinal on Wednesday, prevailing 21-14, 11-21, 21-19 in a contest that lasted 54 minutes, according to reports from the Badminton Association of India carried by MyKhel and Khel Now.

The result guarantees India its first-ever women's singles medal in badminton at the Youth Olympic Games. Whatever happens in the final, Patri will leave with at least a silver medal — a first for an Indian woman in the discipline at this event.

A semifinal that swung both ways

Patri made an impressive start, taking control of the opening game 21-14. Watanabe responded strongly in the second, capitalising on her opportunities to win it 21-11 and force a decider. The third game was a tense, neck-and-neck battle, with neither player willing to concede an advantage. With a place in the final on the line, Patri displayed composure in the closing stages and edged the Japanese shuttler 21-19 to complete a memorable victory.

"The result guarantees India its first-ever women's singles medal in badminton at the Youth Olympic Games."

Why this run is a first

India has enjoyed Youth Olympic badminton success before, but only in boys' singles. HS Prannoy won silver at the inaugural edition in Singapore in 2010, Lakshya Sen finished runner-up in Buenos Aires in 2018, and Aditya Joshi reached the boys' singles semifinals in 2014. No Indian woman had previously gone this far. Patri is now the first Indian woman to reach the final, and only the third Indian overall to play a Youth Olympic badminton gold-medal match.

Patri, who is from Odisha, arrived with strong junior credentials. She is a U17 Badminton Junior Asia champion and also clinched the U15 Asia title in 2024 — a combination no Indian player had previously achieved, winning both continental age-group crowns.

What comes next: Zhang for gold

Patri will now aim to complete her historic campaign with a gold medal against China's Yi Xin Zhang in the final. Zhang enters as a formidable opponent, having recently won gold at the World Junior Championships. The two have met once before, in the quarterfinals of the Asia Junior Championships earlier this year, when Zhang won 21-18, 21-16. The final therefore gives Patri the chance to settle that score on the biggest stage of her young career — and to turn a guaranteed silver into a historic gold.
